cast_dialogue.linea: The third conditional rewrites history, heroes: if + past perfect, would have + participle. Pure imagination about a past that never changed.
If we had left ten minutes later, we would have missed the flight to Tokyo.
If the taxi driver hadn't taken a shortcut, we wouldn't have arrived on time.
And if I hadn't checked the gate, we would have waited at the wrong one!
If you had missed that flight, mis héroes, you would never have seen Mount Fuji at sunrise. Luck loves the brave!

If I hadn't checked the gate, we would have waited at the wrong one.

inicio.definicion_pragmatica: Third conditional imagines an UNREAL past: if + past perfect, would have + past participle. Both halves describe things that did NOT happen. Never use 'would have' in the if-clause.

filas: If we had ✅ / If we would have ❌

ejercicios.afirmacion: The third conditional talks about a past that really happened.
We never use 'would have' in the if-clause.

guion: Sofía: I still can't believe we almost missed the Tokyo flight.
Ben: I know! If we had left ten minutes later, we would have missed it.
Sofía: And if the taxi driver hadn't taken that shortcut...
Ben: We wouldn't have arrived on time. Total disaster.
Sofía: What would you have done?
Ben: I would have cried! And you?

reading.texto: Last summer the friends almost missed their flight to Tokyo. If they had left home ten minutes later, they would have missed it completely. If the taxi driver hadn't taken a shortcut, they wouldn't have arrived on time. And if Kenji hadn't checked the gate, they would have waited at the wrong one. Sofía smiled: 'If we had missed that flight, we would never have seen Mount Fuji at sunrise.'

preguntas.afirmacion: The taxi driver took a shortcut.
Kenji forgot to check the gate.
